auditor: fresh visual auditor, judged from PNGs only
method: Every one of the 15 full-page PNGs was viewed. Comparisons were built as side-by-side composites (source | candidate) sliced into vertical bands at native resolution, plus native-resolution zooms of the nav bar, plan-card feature lists, customer-logo row, comparison-table header, closing CTA and footer. Byte-hashing showed 02==03 (390 current/best identical) and 05==06 (700 current/best identical); classifications below reflect that. Manifest.json was read only to identify which file is which; all classifications here are independent and disagree with it in places.
summary: The reconstruction is faithful at 390 and at 1440 (current). It fails in the middle of the range. At 700 the whole page is frozen in the 390 mobile layout inside a 700 viewport, leaving a dead ~310px black band down the entire 7,714px page. At 1024 and 1100 the shipped build overflows horizontally: the nav is cut off and unusable, a whole plan tier is offscreen, footer columns are truncated, and at 1100 the comparison table loses its header row and three of its four plan columns. The BEST experiment fixes the structural failures at 1024 and 1100 - full nav, all four plan cards on-screen, footer columns restored, comparison-table headings and two extra plan columns restored at 1100 - but it introduces two new visible defects everywhere it acts: the closing CTA headline is forced onto one line and clipped offscreen at 1024/1100, and the customer-logo row collapses into a single jammed cluster with logos physically overlapping at 1024/1100/1440. At 1440, where the shipped build was already correct, BEST is a straight regression.
bestVsCurrentVerdict: Net win at the broken widths, still not clean. Re-audited against the corrected AC5 best images: no width is a BLOCKER any more. AC5 removes both structural failures the previous audit called out - the closing CTA headline wraps to two centred lines and is fully on-screen at 1024/1100/1440, and at 1100 the comparison table renders the complete Features/Free/Basic/Business/Enterprise header with all four value columns on-screen. 1024 goes BLOCKER -> MAJOR and 1100 goes BLOCKER -> MAJOR; 390 and 700 are byte-identical to the shipped build and are unchanged (390 PASS, 700 still the mobile-freeze MAJOR); 1440 is still a regression versus the shipped build (MAJOR) because the customer-logo row collapses there. The blocking defects are gone; what remains is a cluster of horizontal-distribution and vertical-spacing bugs that share one signature - flex justification/gap being lost. Named residuals: (a) the customer-logo row collapses to a zero-gap cluster with the salesforce mark physically overlapping Vercel and Figma at 1024/1100/1440; (b) the header collapses from logo-left/links-right to a centred cluster at 1024/1100/1440; (c) the footer Connect column is clipped mid-word at the right edge at 1100; (d) plan-card feature items and, at 1024, comparison-table value cells lose their row gap and collide when they wrap; (e) the 'Billed yearly' toggle renders as a 4px sliver instead of a pill at 1024/1100/1440. AC5 is adoptable at 1024/1100 on structural grounds and should not be shipped at 1440 in its current form.

bestReaudit.method: Independent re-audit of the replaced best images only. All 15 PNGs were viewed; source-vs-best comparisons were built as side-by-side band composites at every width (proportional bands at 1024 where source is 6,990px and best 6,360px) plus native 1:1 crops of the nav bar, customer-logo row, plan cards, comparison-table header and value cells, closing CTA, and footer right edge. Byte hashes re-confirmed 02==03 at 390 and 05==06 at 700, so AC5 is provably inert at those widths. No classification was carried over from manifest.json or from the earlier audit; the three previously flagged defects were re-checked from the pixels.

newDefectsNotPreviouslyFlagged: Comparison-table value cells lose their row gap and collide when they wrap, at 1024 only: '250 / issues' runs into the '2 teams' row and 'Issues, projects, cycles, / initiatives' runs into 'Customer requests'. The shipped build renders these uncollided.

Header distribution collapses to a centred cluster at 1024 and 1100 as well as 1440 - the logo is no longer anchored to the left margin and the link group is no longer right-aligned. The previous audit noted this only at 1440 and only as 'shifted right and compressed'; it is systemic and shares its root cause with the logo-row collapse.
The 'Billed yearly' control renders as a thin ~4px blue sliver instead of a pill toggle at 1024, 1100 and 1440, in the Basic and Business cards. Source and shipped build both render the full toggle.
notes: The top-level 'summary' field and the per-width 'improvement' fields were left verbatim as instructed; they describe the superseded pre-AC5 best variant and are stale with respect to the CTA-headline and 1100 Enterprise-column findings. 'bestVsCurrentVerdict', 'bestBlockerWidths' and every 'sourceVsBest' block reflect AC5.
All 'sourceVsCurrent' entries were preserved verbatim and were not re-audited.

The remaining AC5 defects share one signature - lost flex justification and lost row gaps - so the logo row, the header bar, the wrapped card/table rows and the collapsed toggle are plausibly one fix, not five.
